business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fitness Biometric Tracking and Wellness Telemetry Apps

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (República de Colombia) - Unitary National Jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition); statutory Commercial Code (Decree 410 of 1971), Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S.), and Administrative Procedure Code (Law 1437 of 2011)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement (FTA with Investor-State Investment Chapter; in force 15 May 2012)
Colombia-United Kingdom Reciprocal Investment Protection Agreement (in force 2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (creation of UIAF - Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero); Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT framework); Law 2010 of 2019 (mandatory UBO register); Decree 2039 of 2020 (UBO regulation); UIAF Resolution 367 of 2021 (UBO identification and reporting thresholds); Resolution DIAN 000086 of 2021 (UBO e-Registry); Decree 1068 of 2015 (single financial regulatory decree incorporating AML/CFT rules); Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S. corporate governance); Decree 410 of 1971 (Commercial Code); Law 1581 of 2012 (personal data protection applicable to health app telemetry); FATF 40 Recommendations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (confidential electronic filing with DIAN and UIAF; not accessible via the public commercial registry)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarial copy of the foreign shareholder's passport (legalized for use in Colombia)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or Consulate of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia is Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention via Law 407 of 2001) OR Consular Legalization for non-Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) for the Colombian incorporation signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the shareholder's jurisdiction or a Colombian Notary if executed in Colombia
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn Spanish translation by an officially registered translator (traductor oficial)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence (Certificado de Vigencia) of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the foreign jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Secretary of State or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the corporate resolution authorizing the Colombian S.A.S. incorporation and appointing the local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary and/or notary of the parent entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn Spanish translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening at onboarding and on a 24-48 hour rolling basis for all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and indirect beneficial owners of the Colombian S.A.S.: (i) OFAC SDN List; (ii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iii) UN Security Council 1267/1988 and 1989/2011 consolidated lists; (iv) UK OFSI Consolidated List; (v) Colombian UIAF Lista Vinculante (PEP and money laundering designated persons); (vi) domestic SARLAFT/SAGRILAFT counterparty lists maintained by Colombian obliged entities. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies automatically to any PEP, sanctions hit, or high-risk jurisdiction finding; screening evidence and negative confirmations must be archived for at least 10 years per Resolution 367 of 2021 and are retained in the corporate pre-incorporation file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social) and the online portals of the network of Cámaras de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), operating under Decreto 1074 of 2015 (Single Commerce Regulatory Decree)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressible in the Spanish alphabet, per Article 10 of the Political Constitution; foreign terms are admitted only when adapted to Spanish phonetic and grammatical rules and written in Latin script; accents, the letter 'ñ', and numerals are permitted; the statutory name must end with the mandatory suffix 'S.A.S.' or the full form 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada'; the RUES homonym database compares exact and phonetically equivalent names, and any spelling variation capable of misleading third parties is deemed conflicting; trade names may include English idioms, but the registered legal name must carry a coherent Spanish transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RUES name reservation is valid for 30 calendar days and may be renewed once for an additional 30 days by written request at the Cámara de Comercio. If the name is rejected (homonym exclusion, prohibited or sensitive token, or administrative discretion), the applicant has 10 working days from notification to file: (i) 'recurso de reposición' with the issuing Cámara de Comercio, and/or (ii) 'recurso de apelación' before the same Cámara, which remits the appeal to the Superintendencia de Sociedades. The appeal must identify the intended name, evidence of prior trademark or brand use, and propose alternative phonetic variants. Under Law 1437 of 2011 (Articles 74-76), the Superintendencia resolves the appeal within two months, extendable by one month for evidentiary review; simultaneously, a fresh RUES search can be launched to reserve an alternate eligible name without waiving the pending appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with material restrictions. The S.A.S. bylaws must state a concrete, verifiable domicile address, which is recorded in the RUES commercial registration. Virtual or serviced office addresses in Bogotá, Medellín, Cali, and Barranquilla are accepted provided the provider maintains signage, reception services, commercial establishment matriculation (Matrícula Mercantil de Establecimiento), and certified forwarding of service of process. A home-office address is allowed for micro software firms. Pure digital mailbox-only addresses and P.O. boxes are rejected. For the fitness biometric tracking and wellness telemetry app business, a physical or hybrid address is strongly recommended to evidence commercial substance, support Habeas Data compliance (Law 1581 of 2012), and facilitate Apple App Store and Google Play developer account verification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 12% annualized probability of an unannounced on-site inspection or address-verification visit by DIAN, the municipal industry-and-commerce tax office, or the Cámara de Comercio during the first 12 months after registration; the probability declines to approximately 5% after two years of consistent RUT, commercial registry, and UBO filings. Inspections are generally triggered by discrepancies between the fiscal address (RUT), the commercial registry address, and the beneficial ownership declaration, rather than by random selection for the low-risk ISIC 6201 software industry.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUES name search and homonym certificate (Certificado de Homónimos)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff fixed by the annual Cámara de Comercio fee schedule; approximately 0.2-0.4 UVT per search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the S.A.S. incorporation document in the Commercial Registry (Inscripción del Documento Privado de Constitución)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee calculated on subscribed capital (approximately 0.7% of capital up to a fixed maximum); estimate assumes subscribed capital below COP 10,000,000 (approximately USD 2,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of the private incorporation document and signatures (autenticación notarial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: National notarial fee table; prevailing market benchmark USD 10-20 per document

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificadas); Código de Comercio, Decreto 410 de 1971, Libro II; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, Título 6
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Registro Único Empresarial (RUES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Único de Registro Empresarial (DUE) y acta constitutiva privada inscrita en el registro mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for S.A.S.; capital is freely determined by shareholders in the bylaws. Paid-in capital is admitted at subscription and no escrow account is required under Colombian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company accepts the subscription of one hundred (100) common shares subscribed and fully paid by the founding shareholder at par value, and that the paid-in capital be deposited in the company's own account with no statutory escrow requirement. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is hereby established at Carrera 7 # 71-21, Office 902, Bogotá D.C., Colombia, and the legal representative is authorized to formalize the lease and administrative registrations. RESOLVED, that Senior Developer Juan Pérez is appointed as President/Manager, and María Gómez as Secretary, with powers to execute routine corporate filings, open bank accounts, and represent the company before the Cámara de Comercio and DIAN. RESOLVED, that all actions taken by the executive officers to implement this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability and Preliminary Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / RUES virtual portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation request through the RUES online system specifying the desired corporate name for an S.A.S. After approval, obtain the certificate of name availability (certificado de homonimia) valid for 30 calendar days. Include the precise corporate purpose of fitness data processing and software development.
required_dossiers: Valid identification document of the requesting shareholder
Authorization letter if submitted by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to homonymy or prohibited similarity, submit up to three alternative names; the registry will re-run the search at no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Private Incorporation Document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / Notary Public (only if real property is contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the private incorporation document (documento privado de constitución) containing the corporate name, domicile, term, shareholders, capital structure, board representation, internal governance rules, and ISIC 6201 business purpose. All founding shareholders must sign before the Cámara de Comercio or a notary; notarial protocol is not mandatory unless real property is contributed to capital.
required_dossiers: Copies of shareholders' identity cards or passports
Proof of legal representation if acting through attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry finds incomplete clauses, correct the document by amendment agreement and re-submit for signature; notarial fees are only incurred when property contributions require certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Mercantile Registry and Obtaining Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Registro Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed incorporation document via RUES, complete Form DUE, and pay the official registration fee. The Cámara de Comercio will issue the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation (certificado de existencia y representación), which perfects the S.A.S. legal personality and enables commencement of operations.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Cámara de Comercio issues an observación, the applicant must adjust the incorporation document within the correction period and resubmit; failure to cure within 10 business days results in file closure and new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification (NIT) and Electronic Invoicing Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) using the certificate of existence, obtaining the NIT. Determine tax classification as responsible for income tax and complementaries, activate electronic invoicing under the DIAN resolution system, and register the legal representative as contact point.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and legal representation
Email address and postal address for tax notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the RUT application, verify NIT and address mismatches, correct information, and re-file online; appointment at DIAN windows may be required for complex cases.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating and Occupational Safety Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oficina de Planeación Municipal / Cuerpo de Bomberos de Bogotá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the Certificado de Uso de Suelo confirming that office-based software development is a permitted use in the selected commercial property. Obtain fire safety inspection and certification for the office premises, and enroll employees with an ARL for occupational risk coverage. Digital health application hosting requires no industrial manufacturing permit.
required_dossiers: Floor plan of the commercial premises
Certificado de Uso de Suelo application
Employees labor contract registration if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection fails, remediate deficiencies (fire extinguishers, emergency exits, alarm systems) within the inspection order deadline; upon structural changes, request a re-inspection by the Bomberos.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo (sectoral oversight only; no industrial license for pure software services)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — cloud-hosted fitness data processing and telemetry apps are excluded from industrial/manufacturing licensing under Colombian commercial regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible / Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical industrial activity; zero point-source discharges generated by the digital health app
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; if office operations generate wastewater or electronic waste, comply with Resolución 631 de 2015 (wastewater parameter limits) and Decreto 4741 de 2005 (hazardous waste management).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from Cuerpo de Bomberos for office premises; structural load inspection certificate (certificado de sismo-resistencia) for leased workspace; workplace occupational safety clearance under the ARL system and Resolución 0312 de 2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN). Portal: https://www.dian.gov.co; transactional and registration portal: MUISCA (https://muisca.dian.gov.co); electronic invoicing platform: https://www.dian.gov.co/FacturaElectronica.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) is formed before a chamber of commerce as a Colombian domestic company. For tax registration, the company, through its legal representative, must apply to DIAN via the MUISCA virtual portal for a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). The procedure is: (1) complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) electronic form identifying the legal form, economic activity ISIC 6201, address, representative, and shareholders; (2) select the tax obligations (income tax, VAT/IVA, credibility in electronic invoicing, withholding taxes); (3) receive and verify the RUT/NIT; (4) obtain a DIAN digital certificate for electronic signatures and enable the 'Resolución de Facturación Electrónica' before issuing invoices. Foreign non-resident shareholders need no individual TIN solely due to shareholding, but must be listed in the RUT where required for transfer pricing, beneficial-ownership and CFC reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Colombian S.A.S. is a resident legal entity subject to corporate income tax (régimen ordinario) on its worldwide income; there is no pass-through treatment for shareholders. The entity is also the direct VAT taxpayer; shareholders are taxed only on dividends/business that may be treated as CET-exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Every S.A.S. is classified as a separate taxable corporation. Optional mechanisms available include: (i) election of the SIMPLE (integrated simple) tax regime under Law 1943/2018 and Decree 1464/2019 for eligible companies with prior-year gross income not exceeding 100,000 UVT, replacing ordinary income and municipal ICA taxes for a compulsory three-year period; (ii) election to treat the entity as a 'IVA responsable' versus a limited 'no responsable' subject under Article 437 E.T., where applicable; and (iii) election to apply tax consolidation or transactional treatments under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule and hybrid mismatch rules, provided the transaction has economic substance. No check-the-box hybrid election is recognized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA) — Impuesto sobre las Ventas under Colombian Tax Code; supplemented by municipal Industria y Comercio (ICA) tax and national consumption tax on certain digital/dematerialized services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VAT registration through the RUT is mandatory for any person undertaking taxable supplies of goods or services in Colombia, irrespective of turnover. A reduced or 'non-responsible' position is available for small traders whose gross ordinary income in the preceding tax period was below 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 174,296,500 for 2025) and who do not engage in taxable imports or specific excluded services; however, an S.A.S. carrying on a digital-health app business must register as a full 'responsable de IVA' because the services are not covered by small-taxpayer exclusions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Colombian VAT-responsible taxpayers must issue electronic invoices (factura electrónica) through DIAN's electronic invoicing system. The invoice must receive real-time validation and clearance via DIAN's platform, either through an authorized technological operating provider or by direct API (web services). Each approved invoice is assigned a CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) or CUDS for electronic credit/debit notes, and the document must also be reported to DIAN with the 'evento electrónico' (electronic acceptance/rejection), ensuring immediate transmission to the tax authority. Export invoices must conspicuously reference the zero-rate and support the export condition.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods and to services used exclusively abroad, including the exporting of software, digital content, cloud services, and mobile app subscription revenue when: (i) the recipient/beneficiary is not domiciled in Colombia; (ii) the service does not involve the exploitation of natural resources in Colombian territory; and (iii) the supplier proves by documentary evidence (contract, store agreements, payment routing, geo-usage logs) that the service is effectively used or available solely abroad. For an S.A.S. operating a fitness tracker, receipts from foreign app-store customers via Apple/Google may be zero-rated, provided the underlying user consumption is physically outside Colombia and no Colombian consumer downloads under local circuits. Recurrent sales to Colombian end-users remain taxable at 19%; non-resident digital intermediaries may themselves owe IVA on the supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Declaración de Exportación formal/electrónica) through DIAN/MUISCA or VUCE, or export certificate in the case of electronic service exports
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or equivalent digital logistics evidence of physical exportation
Commercial export invoice and underlying service contract or app-store settlement statements evidencing the foreign beneficiary
Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de canalización de divisas/declaración de cambio) issued by an authorized Colombian bank showing repatriation under the foreign-exchange regime
Book-tax evidence of app user location, IP/geo usage logs, and merchant/financial settlement data
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN conducts substantive audit scrutiny of zero-rating claims, particularly for intangible/digital exports. Failure to corroborate the foreign-destination requirement triggers reassessment at the standard 19% VAT rate, plus daily default interest and a penalty of up to 160% of the omitted tax. Knowingly false export declarations or fictitious inward remittances may constitute tax fraud (fraude a la resolución de exportaciones) under Colombian criminal law and Law 1762/2015, leading to imprisonment, closure of the exporter, disqualification from VAT refund regimes, and extension of the statute of limitations to up to 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (central bank); its Junta Directiva issues the foreign-exchange regime under Law 9 of 1991, compiled in Resolución Externa 1 de 2018 and Circular Reglamentaria Externa DCIN-83, with joint administration by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) which supervises all authorized 'intermediarios del mercado cambiario' (commercial banks and financial corporations) and by the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) which enforces tax and customs control over cross-border transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso is free-floating with no fixed peg, but Colombia operates a hybrid controlled regime: current-account operations such as service exports, interest payments and dividend remittances must be channeled through the official foreign-exchange market when the amount exceeds the US$5,000 equivalent per operation, while capital-account transactions require prior or simultaneous registration with the Banco de la República and specific Declaración de Cambio formalities. Profit remittance by a non-resident shareholder of an S.A.S. is legally permissible once (i) the foreign direct investment is registered with the Central Bank through the local intermediary, (ii) corporate income tax has been declared and paid, and (iii) the 10% dividend withholding applicable to non-residents has been settled; no additional exchange-control approval is required for the remittance itself, making the COP convertible for dividends but procedurally conditional on registration and tax proof.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of the Mercantile Registry (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the registered seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than March 31 for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs chamber-imposed surcharges and fines; persistent non-renewal may lead to cancellation of the mercantile registration and administrative strike-off of the SAS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Approved by Shareholders (Estados Financieros de Fin de Ejercicio)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Asamblea de Accionistas, then filed with Cámara de Comercio
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must be held by March 31; chamber filing within one month after approval, generally by April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve and file financial statements blocks renewal of the mercantile registration, may produce supervisory sanctions by the Superintendencia de Sociedades, and can lead to forced dissolution or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually according to the DIAN calendar for legal entities, generally between the second half of April and the third week of May, determined by the last two digits of the NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers extemporaneous filing surcharges and monthly default interest; continued non-compliance exposes the company to tax collection proceedings, embargo of assets, and blocking of commercial registration operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner Information (Información de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN through the designated Beneficiario Final form
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in parallel with or prior to the corporate income tax return; any change in ownership or ultimate beneficial ownership is reportable within fifteen (15) business days after becoming known
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission, inaccuracy, or untimely filing of UBO data is subject to DIAN fines; false declarations may cause invalidation of the tax return and prevent issuance of tax compliance certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) is mandatory for an SAS only when (i) total gross assets exceed five thousand (5,000) current monthly legal minimum wages (SMLMV) or (ii) annual gross income exceeds three thousand (3,000) SMLMV, or when the bylaws or law otherwise require it; below these thresholds statutory audit is optional.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed in Colombia (NIIF Plenas) for larger or high-interest entities and NIIF para PYMES (IFRS for SMEs) for the standard digital-health SAS; regulated by Decreto 2420 de 2015 and later modifications.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must validate its identification of ultimate beneficial owners at each fiscal close, reconfirm or update this information with DIAN when filing the annual tax return, and update the shareholder register within the statutory transfer deadline; a 'no change' status is confirmed by filing the reconfirmation, while a share transfer requires a new disclosure to DIAN and a formal minute entry in the share register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Shareholders (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors or Legal Representative Appointments (Libro de Actas e inscripción de directivos)
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 to 4,500 per year for a full statutory audit if threshold is met; without threshold the amount is USD 0 (optional).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday is available to a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada; general rate is flat at 35%. Preferential incentives are limited to the special deduction for research and technological development under Article 158-1 E.T., and the incremental deductions for employee wages of qualifying labor categories under Article 108-1 E.T. The aggregate effective burden on a distributed profit is approximately 38.25% because dividends paid from taxed profits to a non-resident shareholder attract a 5% final dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 - Declaración del impuesto sobre la renta y complementarios; filed electronically at Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) through the MUISCA portal; mandatorily executed using authorized electronic signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ends 31 December. The return is due during the filing calendar period established annually by DIAN for each taxpayer's NIT final digit and the last two digits of the tax year; for a 2025 tax year, deadlines fall between March and April 2026.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the tax year under declaration, e.g. 2025.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian SAS files with its NIT; non-resident shareholders are not inserted in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue recognized in the fiscal year, including App Store revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing before store commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue realized by the Colombian SAS; do not omit store-level commissions, which must be treated as costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 36 - Rentas no constitutivas de renta ni ganancia ocasional
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Items that are not taxable income, such as certain capital reimbursements or exempt dividends received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder cannot shift foreign-source App revenue into this box; domestic source recognition rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary costs, store fees, cloud hosting, salaries, amortization of software, and allowed deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany charges to foreign parent/affiliates must be supported by transfer pricing documentation and cannot create tax-deductible royalty unless economic substance exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after permissible deductions and net operating loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned SAS must compute this on autonomous-basis; no consolidated results are permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 35% income tax on taxable income generated by the SAS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits for potential foreign tax credits on worldwide income do not apply as the company is Colombian resident.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing after the DIAN deadline triggers a fine of 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction, capping at 100% of the tax due and subject to a minimum of 10 UVT. Late filing after an official examination demand is penalized up to 100% of tax due. Daily default interest under Article 635 E.T. is additionally imposed on unpaid tax; substance abuse penalties under Article 671 E.T. can add 50%-100% of the omitted amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividend distributions derived from profits already taxed at the corporate level; 10% on dividend distributions sourced from profits that were exempt or otherwise non-taxed under the Colombian tax regime. Combined with the 35% corporate income tax, the total burden on a taxed-profit dividend is 38.25%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner shareholder must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the country of residence and present it to the Colombian payer before payment or at latest by the annual return filing deadline. For treaty-eligible shareholders, payers apply the reduced rate only after confirming the shareholder is not a fiscally transparent wrapper or conduit, and only where the relevant Colombian tax treaty contains a dividends clause. Failure to file the TRC through the DIAN formal procedure results in the statutory 5%-10% rate applying. Colombia has no comprehensive income tax treaty with the United States; compensation for app-store distribution may require further analysis of royalty characterization.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties paid to non-residents is 15%; treaty-treaty relief may reduce this to 5%-10% where the IP owner holds beneficial ownership. Interest paid to non-residents has a statutory withholding rate of 15%; Colombian treaty rates are typically 5%-10%, subject to TRC and principal-purpose test compliance. Technical and administrative service fees are subject to 15% withholding when rendered from abroad; if linked to a permanent establishment in Colombia, income is instead taxed on a net basis at 35% plus remittance tax treatment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For fiscal year 2025, transfer pricing documentation is mandatory if the Colombian SAS enters into transactions with related parties exceeding 61,000 UVT (UVT 2025 assumed at COP 47,065, thus COP 2,870,965,000), or if its assets exceed 100,000 UVT, or gross income exceeds 61,000 UVT. Master-File preparation is triggered at higher groups where gross income exceeds the 250,000 UVT threshold and where operations exceed 160,000 UVT gross, depending on the latest DIAN interpretation. An Informe Individual and Master File must be filed before the corporate income tax return due date.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulation statute equivalent to a Gulf-cooperation register; however, DIAN applies substance-over-form doctrine, the OECD Principal Purpose Test under DTAs, and anti-abuse rules such as Article 631-3 E.T. (CEBC/crypto reporting) and the abandonment of the CFC exemption for shell holding structures. A health-fitness app company taxed as an SAS must show real business functions, risk-taking, payroll in Colombia, and actual decision-making; a letterbox entity with no premises, staff or local operating activity may be re-characterized as a pass-through conduit, lose treaty benefits, and trigger 35% source taxation plus penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion Via Unreported App Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SAS underdeclares App Store gross revenue or mischaracterizes subscription receipts as non-taxable customer reimbursements; the owner extracts cash as shareholder loans without filing the corresponding annual tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income tax deficiency at 35% plus daily default interest; fraud penalty under Article 671 E.T. of 160% of omitted tax; criminal penalty for tax evasion up to imprisonment and financial fines under the Colombian Criminal Code (Articles 434A and 434D E.T. as incorporated by Law 1819 of 2016).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative or controlling shareholder may be made jointly liable for unpaid taxes under Articles 555-2 and 794 E.T.; the corporate veil may be pierced under SAS Law 1258 of 2008 when assets are fraudulently mixed with shareholder assets, leading to personal restitution, asset freezes, and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised Profit Repatriation via Phantom Intercompany Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SAS pays annual royalties or service fees to a non-resident affiliate for intellectual property that is neither developed nor economically used by the foreign affiliate, or pays a license fee far above arm's length for the fitness app code, effectively disguising a dividend.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disallow the deduction, re-qualify the royalty as a dividend distribution, apply 5%-10% dividend withholding, impose the 100% difference tax, and apply the 40%-100% transfer pricing penalty; if aggravated by sham contracts, criminal fraud penalties attach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who signed the abnormal intercompany contracts are personally liable for the knowing tax disadvantage; imprisonment is available for aggravated tax fraud, and courts can order repayment of the tax deficiency from personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Companies / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SAS exists as a letterbox entity to own App Store subscription rights, maintain a Colombian premise but no employees, and enter into back-to-back arrangements with a foreign parent; or the company claims treaty benefits without demonstrating principal purpose and business substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN can disregard the legal structure, attribute actual income to the beneficial owner in Colombia, assess 35% corporate tax plus penalty for inaccuracy (up to 100% of tax due), and impose withholding tax on any deemed dividend distribution. Tax residence itself can be challenged when central management and control is outside Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director failing to petition liquidation or activ it cannot escape shadow management; under the veil-piercing doctrine the shareholder may be ordered to pay corporate debts, and a criminal court may issue a material travel embargo while tax fraud charges are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and IAP Revenue Channel Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SAS channels revenues from Apple IAP and Google Play through anonymous or non-identifiable accounts, fails to keep accounting records of app commissions, or knowingly processes chargebacks and unauthorized digital-health subscription proceeds in a way that obscures the beneficial owner's identity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Colombian Anti-Money Laundering regime (Law 1990 of 2019 and Circular DIAN/Superfinanciera) exposes the company to pecuniary fines of up to 1.5 billion COP for missing suspicious transaction reporting; administrative closure of the NIT and registry entry in the fraud database may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company directors can be personally fined for not adopting a formal AML compliance framework; if app-store proceeds are laundered through shell companies or cryptocurrencies, bank accounts freeze, assets are forfeited, and imprisonment from 4 to 12 years applies.
